To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have presented a formalism which can be used to factorize and sum up rapidity logarithms, which has been applied to a wide class of physical processes, and which is gauge invariant.

we introduce a new framework to resum rapidity logarithms, we show how to factorize and sum rapidity logarithms to all orders in perturbative QCD, and we present a new definition of TMDPDFs that is gauge invariant and independent of the hard process.
we have presented a formalism which can factorize and resummate observables in a gauge invariant way and which allows one to track scheme dependence in the process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a formalism to systematically treat rapidity logarithms which arise in QCD.
the systematic treatment of the resummation and factorization of rapidity divergent quantities in QCD.
the development and application of new techniques for the systematic treatment and resummation of observables which involve rapidity logarithmics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formalism we present here allows for a systematic treatment of the resummation and factorization of observables in QFT which involve rapidity divergencies.

we have presented a formalism for resumming rapidity logarithms, which is applicable to a large variety of observables and which allows for a systematic treatment of the scheme dependence inherent to such resummations.
the formalism presented here allows for a consistent and systematic factorization and resummation of all rapidity diverg- ences in QCD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a systematic and universal formalism to factorize and re- sum rapidity diverg- ences.
we have presented a formalism which provides a systematic treatment of rapidities, and allows us to resum rapidity logarithms to all orders in perturbation theory.
we have provided the first formalism for the factorization of observables sensitive to soft recoil and the resummation thereof.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rapidity diverg- ences are a natural feature of quantum field theory which are best treated with the notion of a rapidity renormalization group.
one can systematically treat rapidity logarithms using a renormalization scheme which is universal across a wide variety of observables.
a rapidity renormalization group provides a natural framework to factorize observables which have rapidity logarithms.
